title: [FEATURE] Add keyboard shortcut for switching between Code sessions in Claude Desktop
body:
### Problem Statement

I'm migrating from Claude Code CLI to Claude Desktop's Code feature. In the CLI, my terminal gives me tabs I can cycle through with keyboard shortcuts (e.g., `Cmd+Shift+]`/`Cmd+Shift+[`). Claude Desktop already has a session list in the sidebar, but there's no keyboard shortcut to cycle through sessions — I have to click each one with the mouse.

### Proposed Solution

Add keyboard shortcuts to cycle through Code sessions in the sidebar (e.g., `Cmd+Shift+]`/`Cmd+Shift+[`), matching the convention used by most terminal emulators and browsers for tab switching.

### Alternative Solutions

Arrow key navigation within the session list when it has focus would also work.

### Priority

Medium - Would be very helpful

### Feature Category

Interactive mode

### Use Case Example

Coming from the CLI, I'm used to switching between sessions entirely with the keyboard via terminal tab shortcuts. The session list already exists in Claude Desktop's sidebar — it just needs a keyboard-driven way to navigate it.

**Related: #45698 — "Expose session navigation as bindable actions in keybindings.json"**

That issue requests the same capability at the CLI/TUI layer via `~/.claude/keybindings.json`. The two are complementary:

- This issue covers **Claude Desktop** (Electron app, system-level shortcut, GUI sidebar navigation) — works out of the box for all Desktop users
- #45698 covers the **CLI/TUI** (`keybindings.json` `session:*` actions) — opt-in for power users who already customize their bindings

top_comments.body:
+1 on this request. Coming from KDE/Konsole and browser muscle memory, I'd suggest Ctrl+PgUp / Ctrl+PgDn as the default binding for cycling through Code sessions in Claude Desktop. This matches:

- Browser tab cycling (Chrome, Firefox)
- Konsole tab cycling (KDE default)
- Most terminal emulators on Linux

It's a more universal convention than Cmd+Shift+]/[ (macOS-only), and would feel immediately natural to Linux desktop users. The tabs:next / tabs:previous actions already exist in the keybindi
